subject.title: Feature: Add denylist support for exec-approvals

question: Should OpenClaw adopt the linked PR's deny-over-allow design, including both `tools.exec.denylist` and exec-approvals-file rules, as the permanent cross-host execution-approval contract?
rationale: This introduces persistent configuration and defines precedence, prompting, revocation, and failure behavior at a security boundary; source correctness cannot determine whether two policy owners are an acceptable product contract.

options.title: Consolidate then land
options.body: Choose one canonical policy owner or explicitly define deterministic layering, then resolve the conflict and require exact-head cross-host proof before merge.

options.title: Accept both surfaces
options.body: Land the dual-surface design after documenting precedence and proving fresh-install, upgrade, gateway, node, and companion behavior.

options.title: Keep policy external
options.body: Decline native expansion, close the implementation PR, and direct users to maintained policy plugins such as CRE or SafeClaw.

recommendation.title: Consolidate then land
recommendation.body: Choose one canonical policy owner or explicitly define deterministic layering, then resolve the conflict and require exact-head cross-host proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: This person introduced the exec host approval flow, has the strongest continuing history on its central policy paths, and participated in the issue's prior review.
